verses.text: In the spring, the time when kings go off to war, David sent out Joab with his officers and the whole army of Israel. They destroyed the Ammonites and surrounded the city of Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
One evening David got up from his bed and walked around on the roof of the palace. From the roof he saw a woman bathing. She was very beautiful.
David sent someone to find out who she was. The man said, "Isn't this Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam and wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
Then David sent messengers to bring her. She came to him, and he slept with her. She had just finished the washing that made her clean after her monthly period. Then she went back home.
The woman became pregnant, and she sent a message to David: "I am pregnant."
So David sent a message to Joab: "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
When Uriah came, David asked him how Joab was, how the soldiers were, and how the war was going.
Then David said to Uriah, "Go home and wash your feet and rest." Uriah left the palace, and the king sent a gift after him.
But Uriah did not go home. He slept at the door of the palace with all his master's servants.
David was told, "Uriah did not go home." So David said to Uriah, "You have just come back from a journey. Why didn't you go home?"

Uriah said to David, "The ark and the armies of Israel and Judah are staying in tents. My master Joab and your officers are camping in the open fields. How could I go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? As surely as you live, I will not do such a thing!"
Then David said to Uriah, "Stay here one more day, and tomorrow I will send you back." So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.
David invited him to eat and drink with him, and David got him drunk. But in the evening Uriah went out to sleep on his mat among his master's servants. He still did not go home.
The next morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.
In the letter he wrote, "Put Uriah at the front, where the fighting is worst. Then pull back from him so that he will be struck down and die."
So while Joab was surrounding the city, he put Uriah at a place where he knew the enemy's strongest fighters were.
The men of the city came out and fought against Joab. Some of David's soldiers were killed, and Uriah the Hittite also died.
Then Joab sent David a full report about the battle.
He told the messenger, "When you finish telling the king everything about the battle,
the king may become angry and ask you, 'Why did you go so close to the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?

Who killed Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Wasn't it a woman who threw a large millstone down on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?' If he asks this, then tell him, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead too.'"
So the messenger went and told David everything Joab had sent him to say.
The messenger said to David, "The enemy was stronger than us. They came out to fight us in the open field, but we pushed them back to the entrance of the city gate.
Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall. Some of the king's men were killed, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead too."

David said to the messenger, "Tell Joab this: 'Don't let this upset you. The sword kills one person as easily as another. Attack the city more strongly and destroy it.' Encourage Joab with these words."
When Uriah's wife heard that her husband Uriah was dead, she mourned for him.
When the time of mourning was over, David sent for her and brought her to his palace. She became his wife and had a son by him. But the LORD was not pleased with what David had done.
